title: D3b: delegation ceiling and self-expiring credentials for coordinator-to-subagent dispatch
description: Operator ruled YES on D3 (2026-08-17). Two properties, enforced structurally rather than by policy: no identity may delegate more privilege than it holds; and a subagent credential carries a TTL the subagent cannot extend. Coordinator-to-subagent dispatch is unconstrained today. W-002 already carries an expiry, so make the expiry the rule rather than the instance. Write down the honest limit: under D-17 every agent runs as the same OS user, so this bounds ACCIDENT and makes overreach attributable, and does not bound an adversary. Pin it with a test that tries to exceed the ceiling and shows what is and is not stopped.

notes.note:
HANDOFF -> verifier: T-401 (D3b) DONE by coordinator-opus, handing to a DISTINCT verifier. Two things the
verifier should go at first are in sections 3 and 5: a defect this change CREATES, and a
property it must not have broken.

1. WHAT WAS BUILT

A `grant` act delegates a SUBSET of a name's privileges for a BOUNDED time. Because `grant`
was already made a privileged kind in T-400, delegating now requires a declared intent
first -- that composition was not arranged for tidiness: delegation is exactly the act whose
deliberation belongs on the record before it happens.

New: delegated_keys(), signing_keys(), held_kinds(), effective_expiry(), grant_privilege(),
delegations(). CLI: grant, delegations, holds. sign_act now enforces the ceiling and the
expiry at signing time.

WHAT IS STOPPED. Granting a kind you do not hold. Granting past your own expiry. Granting to
yourself. Granting to a warranted name. A second grant to a name that already holds a
credential (refused, NOT merged -- merging is how a ceiling gets raised one act at a time).
Signing a kind you were not granted. Signing after expiry. Re-delegating without holding
`grant`.

2. A GAP THE TESTS FOUND, WORTH KNOWING THE SHAPE OF

The first implementation checked only that the delegated KINDS were a subset of the
grantor's. IT NEVER CHECKED THAT THE GRANTOR HELD `grant` ITSELF. So any delegate could
re-delegate forever: the ceiling bounded WHAT was passed on and left WHETHER it could be
passed on unbounded. Half a ceiling. A credential is now non-re-delegable by default and
handing on the power to hand on is an explicit decision.

A second gap, same origin: warrant.enrolled_keys never returned `valid_until`, so
effective_expiry returned None for every warranted name AND NOTHING WAS CLAMPED. A
hand-written grant could outlive the warrant it descended from. Fixed by adding the field
in warrant.py, derived from the same already-verified payload as every other field there --
so no new trust is placed anywhere. The alternative was re-verifying every warrant a second
time inside attest.py, duplicating that loop and its refusals. VERIFIER: that is the one
edit in warrant.py; check it places no new trust.

3. THE DEFECT THIS CHANGE CREATES. NAMED, NOT HIDDEN.

DELEGATION-OUTSIDE-RECONCILE-A. `warrant.py reconcile` asks whether every ROLL row traces to
a verified warrant, and that property is what lets warrant.py say minting is closed
(conditionally). A delegated identity holds no plaza and is in no roll, so RECONCILE REPORTS
CLEAN WHILE A DELEGATED IDENTITY CAN SIGN. A test demonstrates exactly that.

That is reconcile answering a narrower question, not reconcile failing. But an auditor who
runs only reconcile now gets an incomplete answer to "who can sign here". `attest.py
delegations` is the corresponding report and the ONLY place these identities are enumerated;
its output says both verbs must be run and neither alone is the answer.

VERIFIER: decide whether that split is acceptable or whether reconcile must be widened. The
coordinator did NOT widen it, deliberately -- reconcile's guarantee is stated in terms of
warranted names and quietly changing what that word covers would break the guarantee while
appearing to strengthen it. That reasoning is the thing to attack.

4. THE TTL, AND WHY "CANNOT EXTEND ITSELF" IS TRUE RATHER THAN INTENDED

Two INDEPENDENT barriers, because one is walkable:
  (a) a name cannot grant to itself -- refused at sign time;
  (b) every expiry is clamped to the grantor's ON READ, so no path through the graph produces
      a date later than the warrant at its root.
Barrier (b) is the one that matters. test_a_credential_cannot_be_extended_through_an_
intermediary_either has sub-m grant to sub-n and sub-n try to mint something longer;
test_a_forged_longer_expiry_is_clamped_on_read rewrites a grant by hand to 2100, re-signs it
so it VERIFIES, and asserts the credential still expires with W-001 in 2099. Sign-time
refusals only bind the shipped verb, which is why the read side clamps too.

Expiry is REFUSED at grant time, never clamped. Silently keeping a smaller value than the
caller typed is defect T-376's exact shape, and here the value is a SECURITY parameter.

5. THE PROPERTY THAT MUST NOT HAVE BROKEN

warrant.enrolled_keys STILL MEANS WARRANTED ONLY. signing_keys is the wider set, and every
call site inside attest.py was moved to it deliberately. If a grant could add to
enrolled_keys, reconcile's roll-traces-to-warrant check would be reasoning over
agent-created identities and "minting is closed" would be false.
test_warrant_enrolled_keys_is_not_widened_by_a_grant is the fence. Verify the fence is
actually where the fence needs to be.

Nothing is minted outside the warrant tree either: a grant act lives on a warranted name's
chain, which traces to a warrant, which traces to the operator's key. The tree got DEEPER,
not wider.

6. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BOUND, DEMONSTRATED AND NOT ASSERTED

test_the_ceiling_is_bypassed_entirely_by_reading_the_grantors_key. A subagent holding only
`verdict` that wants `contest` does not attack the ceiling -- it reads the grantor's private
key off the filesystem, because every agent runs as the same OS user (D-17), and signs as the
grantor, who holds everything. The test asserts THIS WORKS. It must keep passing. If it ever
fails, someone has claimed a wall this module does not have.

The ceiling bounds ACCIDENT and makes overreach ATTRIBUTABLE. DIS-2 is the only real
consolation: the forged privilege credits the grantor, never the subagent that wanted it.

AND IT IS VACUOUS AT THE FIRST HOP. A warranted name holds every privileged kind, because
nothing in this harness restricts a warranted name by role yet. So the ceiling constrains
re-delegation and NOT the coordinator's first grant. Pinned by a test so the limitation
cannot quietly be forgotten. Anyone citing D3b as a bound on a warranted name is citing
something that does not exist.

7. EVIDENCE, REPLAYABLE

  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/ -q                          -> 589 passed, 4 skipped
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_attest_delegation.py -q  -> 27 passed
  python3 .harness/bin/attest.py delegations   -> 9 warranted, 0 delegated, depth 0, and it
                                                 prints DELEGATION-OUTSIDE-RECONCILE-A itself
  python3 .harness/bin/attest.py holds --name revision-doctrina
       -> expires 2026-11-10T00:00:00Z, which is W-002's own expiry. That is the live proof
          the valid_until fix works: every one of the nine seated names' signing authority
          ends with the warrant, on the date aligned to the T-349 quarterly watch.
  python3 .harness/bin/warrant.py reconcile    -> still clean, unchanged

SIX NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each in a COPY of .harness, never the live tree:
  A read-side ceiling not intersected      -> 1 fail (the transitive test; correct, the
                                              read-side ceiling only bites at depth 2+)
  B sign-time ceiling removed              -> 2 fail
  C expiry clamped instead of refused      -> 2 fail
  D read-side expiry clamp removed         -> 1 fail
  E expired credentials still resolve      -> 1 fail
  F sign_act stops enforcing held kinds    -> 1 fail

8. NO LIVE WRITE WAS PERFORMED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE

T-400's handoff section 6 records the coordinator signing a false verdict onto the live chain
while smoke-testing. This time the live checks were READ-ONLY (delegations, holds, reconcile)
and the write path is covered by the suite instead. There are no new acts on any live chain
from T-401. Verify that: `attest.py trace` should still show only revision-doctrina's three
acts from T-400, and no grants anywhere.

9. KNOWN COST, STATED NOW

delegated_keys verifies every grant signature on every call, and one sign_act reaches it
several times. O(acts x depth) per call, milliseconds at 9 names and single-digit acts. If the
chains grow it needs a PER-CALL MEMO and not a persisted cache -- a memo inside one call
cannot go stale, a file can, and that is the roster.py agent_keys defect.
